reason: Start with the active-loop FMOPA reorder: it preserves each tile’s FP32 update order and adds no packing or allocation. Next test branch placement, then guarded prefetch; both are small active-path changes, though prior loop-schedule and prefetch experiments did not show repeatable gains and those measurements targeted different code. Scratch padding and B repacking change memory layout and add address or packing costs. The two B-panel proposals are closely related and both carry a 1 MiB packing cost. Transpose fusion repeats A reads across column panels. A transpose fusion for fallback sizes does not affect the fixed n=512 timing. No proposal has measured evidence of a gain.
